lines.text: The largest island of the Caribbean, shaped by sugar, slavery, revolution and its giant neighbour to the north. This is the story of Cuba.
Long before Europeans came, the Taino people farmed and fished across Cuba and the great islands around it.
In 1492 Christopher Columbus reached the Caribbean and landed on Cuba, and the island's world was changed for ever.
In 1519 the Spanish founded Havana, which grew into a great port where treasure fleets gathered for the voyage home.
Centuries of Spanish rule followed. In 1853 Jose Marti was born, the poet who would become the voice of Cuban freedom.
In 1868 Cubans rose against Spain in the Ten Years' War, the first great fight for independence.
In 1895 Marti's war began again, and he was killed in one of its first battles, becoming a national hero.
In 1898 the United States joined in, and Spanish rule over Cuba came to an end.
In 1901 Fulgencio Batista was born, the soldier who would later rule Cuba as a dictator.
That year the United States passed the Platt Amendment, keeping the right to step into Cuban affairs.
In 1902 Cuba became an independent republic, though it lived in the shadow of the United States.
A year later the Americans leased Guantanamo Bay in the south-east for a naval base. They are there still.
In 1926 Fidel Castro was born, the young lawyer who would lead a revolution and rule Cuba for almost fifty years.
Two years later in Argentina came Che Guevara, the doctor who would fight beside him.
And in 1931, Fidel's brother Raul, who would one day take over from him.
In 1953 the revolution began with an attack on an army barracks. Six years later Batista fled, and Castro's rebels took power.
Relations with Washington soon broke down, and an American ban on trade with Cuba began that lasts to this day.
In 1960, Miguel Diaz-Canel was born, the first leader of Cuba born after the revolution.
In April 1961 Cuban exiles backed by the CIA landed at the Bay of Pigs. They were defeated, and Cuba drew closer to Moscow.
The next October, American planes found Soviet missiles in Cuba. For thirteen days the world stood near nuclear war, until they were removed.
In 1980 about a hundred and twenty-five thousand Cubans left from the port of Mariel by boat for Florida.
When the Soviet Union fell, its aid stopped, and Cuba entered the Special Period, years of hunger and shortages.
Then in 1996, a group of veteran musicians recorded old Cuban songs as the Buena Vista Social Club, and the world fell in love.
In 2014 Presidents Obama and Raul Castro announced that the two countries would restore relations.
And in 2021 thousands took to the streets in the largest protests since the revolution.
From the Taino to today, Cuba's story is one of an island that would not stay quiet.
